title: 5-toubun no Hanayome Movie
content:
As an avid fan of the Anime, it was odd for even me to dismiss watching this movie for years until now. Part of it was that I thought was going to be filler, so why not wait for a canon release and then watch this as an appetizer. I guess I was wrong and dismissful.

But alas, even after watching this and even as big of a fan I was of season one and two, tagging along this movie felt very unfamiliar and kind grueling, off putting during some scenes that I started to doze off and think to myself, “did I just mature or has the show always been this … unseasoned”.

I’ll come across and say it, spoiler talk starts from here.

This was the awaited finale of the Quintuplets saga, as unexciting as it is, it was the kind of show that show not have an ending, an infinitely ongoing soap opera of harem that just keeps on giving, but that was too much to hope fore. I although, I would admit, the finale did end up aligning to my Yotsuba agenda, it really felt kind of uninspired and as if it dozed off so much potential in between. All in all and in my extreme limited opinion, this show had a couple more season in it.

As someone who has started as a strong team Miku defender, who later switched teams towards Nino because of certain episodes, only to finally see the light oozing from Yotsuba’s side, I wished to see more spice, more drama and more rivalry that does not shy past the “eternal sibling love”, I wanted a dumpster fire, the likes of Domestic na Kanojo, but I’ll give it to the Mangaka, there was a set vision from the start that never straight off the plan path, you could see in retrospect how the story was going to end, and with this movie, you can feel it even more. The dreaded end in sight, and you just can’t let go just yet.

For a two hours movie, I’ll give some applause to the pacing. There was definitely a cut in the middle, separating the two major arcs, the school festival and the final confessions. The first half is definitely a game of hide and seek, almost, with constant back and forth between multiple perspectives of the same three festival days, each uncovering a little more into the psyche of the quintuplets, almost having them spell it out for you, the end is near and even them are aware of it, it makes them desperate for a trophy snag, but so many shackles pin them down to certain degrees. There was one very rushed, very stupid in my opinion, plot point that they decided to cram in there, it had to do with the girls’ biological father. It is undoubtedly the weakest part of not just the movie, but the entire series, it was just out of nowhere and all around creepy for a few implications, completely threw me off in the middle, but aside from that and the bittersweet final weeding moments, the movie was an all-around solid quintuplet extravaganza that I should have definitely watched way sooner.

Overall: 7.84/10.
